name: Oracle OCI 'GPU - Accelerated Compute' price table, including AMD MI300X and MI355X per-GPU-hour rates
notes:
Observed 2026-10-05, USD. The section headed '#### GPU - Accelerated Compute' carries the column 'GPU price per hour*' with the page's own footnote '\* The server price per hour is calculated by multiplying the GPU price per hour by the number of GPUs.' — i.e. these are PER-GPU rates, not per-node rates, which is the unit fact this repo most often gets wrong.

Full table as read 2026-10-05 (shape | GPUs | GPU price per hour): BM.GPU.RTXPro.8 | 8x RTX PRO 6000 96GB | $4.50; BM.GPU.B200.8 | 8x B200 180GB | $14.00; BM.GPU.GB200.41 | 4x B200 189GB (NVL72) | $16.00; BM.GPU.GB300.42 | 4x B300 279GB (NVL72) | $18.00; BM.GPU.B300.8 | 8x B300 263GB | $15.00; BM.GPU.H200.8 | 8x H200 141GB | $10.00; BM.GPU.H100.8 | 8x H100 80GB | $10.00; BM.GPU.MI300X.8 | 8x AMD MI300X 192GB | $6.00; BM.GPU.MI355X.8 | 8x AMD MI355X 288GB | $8.60; BM.GPU.A100-v2.8 | 8x A100 80GB | $4.00; BM.GPU.L40S.4 | 4x L40S 48GB | $3.50; BM.GPU4.8 | 8x A100 40GB | $3.05; BM.GPUA10.4 | 4x A10 | $2.00; VM.GPU.A10.1 | 1x A10 | $2.00; VM.GPU3.x | V100 16GB | $2.95; VM.GPU2.1 | P100 | $1.275.

THE FINDING THIS SOURCE EXISTS FOR: Oracle publishes a per-GPU-hour price for AMD Instinct MI300X ($6.00) and MI355X ($8.60). This directly contradicts the repo's standing claim, recorded in docs/08-cost-per-token.md section 'What the records cannot answer yet' item 2 and echoed by tools/cost_per_token.py gaps output in 11 separate places, that 'no supply record prices AMD Instinct per GPU-hour' and that this is 'the highest-value gap in the repo'. That claim was true when written and is now false. Oracle prices NVIDIA H100 at $10.00 and AMD MI300X at $6.00 on the same page in the same column, so the two are directly comparable.

Verified by TWO INDEPENDENT methods on 2026-10-05: (1) server-rendered HTML fetched as text, which returns the table with prices intact; (2) the live rendered DOM read through a browser, querying every table row and returning innerText, which returned the literal rows 'BM.GPU.MI300X.8 8x AMD MI300X 192 GB Matrix Core CDNA 3 8x1x400 Gb/sec RDMA $6.00' and 'BM.GPU.MI355X.8 8x AMD MI355X 288GB Matrix Core CDNA 4 8x1x400 Gb/sec RDMA $8.60'. A third path, a plain-text reader proxy, returned the shape names but DROPPED the price column — a reminder that a text extractor can silently lose exactly the field a price record exists to carry, which is the same class of defect as the Cerebras false negative in this repo's history.
